title: Dental Assistant Salary Guide: What Could You Earn?
summary: Dental assisting is a hands-on technical health sciences career that is an important job in any dental practice.
body_markdown:
Dental assisting is a hands-on technical health sciences career that is an important job in any dental practice. These essential workers support dentists by preparing patients, assisting the dentist during procedures, sterilizing equipment, and handling administrative tasks. This multifaceted job[has a bright outlook in job demand nationwide](https://www.onetonline.org/help/bright/31-9091.00) , and this salary guide can give you a good understanding of your earning potential and growth opportunities.


## How Much Do Dental Assistants Make?


Dental assistants currently have a national salary range of $37,130 to $62,350, with an annual average of $48,0701. The projected growth in job demand of 7% is much higher than average2.


There are many factors that can increase salary, such as work experience, earning specialized certifications, job demand and regional economic conditions, which we detail in the rest of this article.


### Factors That Influence A Dental Assistant’s Salary


#### What Regions Have Higher Than Average Pay?


Pay can vary significantly depending on what part of the country a dental assistant works in. Salaries for dental assistants in Minnesota, Massachusetts, Oregon, the District of Columbia and New Hampshire[range from $54,190 to $62,760](https://www.bls.gov/oes/2023/may/oes319091.htm#:~:text=Top%20paying%20states%20for%20Dental%20Assistants) , well above the national mean average salary of 48,0701. There are some large metropolitan areas outside of the 5 top-paying states that also offer higher than the national average, specifically the California cities of[San Jose, Sunnyvale, Santa Clara, Santa Rosa, and San Francisco areas](https://www.bls.gov/oes/2023/may/oes319091.htm#:~:text=Top%20paying%20metropolitan%20areas%20for%20Dental%20Assistants) .


#### Dental Assistant Licensing, Certifications and Specialized Training


There is no national licensure for dental assistants at the federal level, and states set their own requirements for the certifications needed to be employed as a dental assistant. You can check your[state’s requirements on the Dental Assisting National Board website](https://www.danb.org/state-requirements) .


Most states require dental assistants to be either licensed, registered, or certified for entry or advancement in the field of dental assisting. Some states may require assistants to hold[specific advanced certifications](https://www.danb.org/certification/earn-dental-assistant-certification) in order to work in dental radiography (x ray), dental sedation, or other extended functions. For specific requirements in your state, contact the State Board of Dental Examiners.


To earn a certification, applicants must pass the certification exam for each specific specialty that they want to pursue. The educational requirements for certification are that dental assistants must either have graduated from an accredited program or have a high school diploma and complete the required amount of work experience. Dental assistants must have current certification in cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR). Additional information about certifications can be found at[CareerOneStop](https://www.careeronestop.org/Toolkit/Training/find-certifications.aspx?keyword=31-9091&ajax=0&direct=0) .


#### Typical Employers of Dental Assistants


The majority of dental assistants are employed at dental practices, while a smaller number of dental assistants work at physician’s offices, outpatient care facilities, as well as for federal, state and local governments3.


## Frequently Asked Questions About Dental Assistant Salaries


**Do Dental Assistants Earn More In Specialized Dental Practices?**


Yes, they can, with the right certifications. Examples of[dental specialties include Oral surgery, Orthodontics, Endodontics, Periodontics](https://www.danb.org/news-blog/detail/blog/how-a-dental-assistants-practice-can-affect-their-pay) and more.


**Is Dental Assisting Considered a Good-Paying Career?**


Dental assisting may be particularly attractive career choice for individuals interested in healthcare, patient care, and working in a dental environment. Earning special certifications can also add to job satisfaction. According to the BLS, employment of dental assistants is projected to grow 7% between 2025 and 2035, faster than the average projected growth for all occupations2.
